I put the quotation marks around Cinderella since the tale I am looking at is the German tale of Aschenputtel and I honestly didn't bother too much for picking up potential minor differences between the versions. Also I am looking at a very old version that utilized the typical trope Aschenputtel is know for. I doubt the stuff I am writing will be very scientific and probably quite a stretch sometimes, but I hope it will be fun. It's also the first time I am writing this down and it might be long, so bear with me please. It might be worth it.
As my main source I used the German book "Lexikon der Zaubermärchen" by Walter Scherf.

Let's start:

The Swiss-born priest and preacher Johann Geiler von Kaysersberg (1445 – 1510) already knew the story of Aschenputtel, but apparently he also knew a much older story which utilizes many of the characteristics used in Aschenputtel. This tale goes back to the 5th century!

It is important to know that the pronoun describing Eschengrüdel used in the original telling in German is masculine, simply because the term "Eschengrüdel" is masculine. Keep in mind that this in no way has to indicate the sex of the person being the Eschengrüdel.

This tale is about Eschengrüdel. The loyal Eschengrüdel works in the kitchen of a nunnery, but the nuns play evil pranks on him. They pour water over him, beat him and smear mustard in his nose. Eventually an angle shows an holy old man the way to the nunnery so he can demonstrate an example of perfection. When the can arrives all girls are called, but the girl from his dreams is missing. They tell him everyone is there, besides the fool in the kitchen. The Eschengrüdel is called and appears with bandaged head apparently because it didn't want to show its hair.

There obviously are many red flags in this. The first one is Johann Geiler von Kaysersberg himself. Kaysersberg was famous for his speeches about witchcraft, superstition and witches. I'm not entirely sure what his stance in witchcraft was, but he was at least in some way connected to it. The next obvious one is the holy old man. I believe the priest changed Odin to and old holy man in the Christian sense. The angles could simply be his ravens. Fitting, I'd say.

Now Odin reaches the nunnery and calls all women together and eventually encounters Eschengrüdel. The whole reason for Odin to go the nunnery was to reveal something about Eschengrüdel and considering her hair is explicitly mentioned too be hidden I think his purpose was the reveal exactly this hair. Why the hair?

The hair represents fertility and femininity. How so? Loki cuts of Sif's (Thor's wife) hair, representing the burning of growth through fire. The growth itself is the wife to rain, was Sif is the wife to Thor. I think Eschengrüdel was revealed as a women by Odin and that the dirty tricks were played on her because she was considered to be a man by the rest. This also explains the strange use of pronouns in the tale and is extremely relevant to why it was Odin who revealed her.

We know Loki accuses Odin of effeminate behaviour, passive homosexuality and the ritual change of his sex in the Lokasenna in the context of Seidr, basically witchcraft (Kaysersberg!).

I think Eschengrüdel also ritually changed her sex in order to practice Seidr and was consequently mocked because the change was to perfect to be noticed by the women around her who thought it was a man practising the craft. This also fits with the purpose of Odin wanting to demonstrate an example of perfection. The perfection was Eschengrüdel.

Another interesting aspect is the name of Eschengrüdel. The German name, Aschenputtel, is thought to describe a dirty women digging in ashes. In English Ash both describes the tree and the burned remains. In German that is not the case: burned remains are called "Asche", as our protagonist in the modern tale, the tree however is called Esche. Imagine that.
In the widely known version we even have a tree which is helping our beloved Cinderella. So I'd even go as far as saying we have a connection to Yggdrasil, the tree Odin hung himself on in order to gain wisdom.

tl:dr: I think Cinderella was practising Seidr and Odin gives his approval.
